package_info.package_manager: source distribution (also repackaged in Maven Central and other ecosystems)
package_info.why_malicious: OpenSSL versions 3.0.0 through 3.0.6 contain a critical security vulnerability (CVE-2022-3602 and CVE-2022-3786) that allows attackers to exploit buffer overflows during X.509 certificate verification, potentially leading to remote code execution or denial of service. This vulnerability can compromise the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of systems relying on OpenSSL for cryptographic operations. The issue is resolved in version 3.0.7.

behavioral_signatures: Detection of OpenSSL library versions 3.0.0 through 3.0.6 loaded in memory or present on disk during cryptographic operations.
Applications or services (including Java applications via JNI or wrapper packages) dynamically or statically linking to OpenSSL 3.0.0 - 3.0.6.
Processes performing X.509 certificate validation using vulnerable OpenSSL versions.
file_indicators: Presence of libssl.so.3 or libcrypto.so.3 with version 3.0.0 - 3.0.6 in system library paths (e.g., /usr/lib/, /usr/local/lib/).
Java wrapper packages in Maven Central or other repositories that bundle OpenSSL 3.0.0 - 3.0.6 (e.g., netty-tcnative, tcnative-boringssl-static).
Application dependency manifests (pom.xml, requirements.txt, etc.) referencing OpenSSL 3.0.0 - 3.0.6.
network_indicators: No static network indicators; exploitation may involve malformed or maliciously crafted TLS handshakes or X.509 certificates targeting vulnerable OpenSSL instances.
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Perform a comprehensive inventory of all systems and application dependencies to identify OpenSSL versions 3.0.0 through 3.0.6. Use software composition analysis (SCA) tools to scan for both direct and transitive dependencies, including native libraries and Java wrapper packages. Examine system library directories for vulnerable OpenSSL binaries. Monitor for vendor advisories and apply security patches (upgrade to OpenSSL 3.0.7 or later) immediately. Additionally, review application logs for unusual certificate validation errors or crashes that may indicate exploitation attempts.
